tasks.short: Check production documents, materials and work processes against specifications.

steps.what: Find the applicable specification revision and inspection checklist.
Check production documents for required fields, quantities, signatures and specification references.

loop.input: Production documents and an approved checklist of required evidence.
loop.output: Cited field values and locations of signatures, with missing or unreadable evidence flagged.
loop.check: Apply deterministic completeness and consistency rules; clerk verifies flagged evidence. Signature presence does not prove validity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per document; unreadable or contradictory evidence goes to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scanned forms and narrative entries lack consistent fields; structured documents use direct checks.

steps.what: Inspect materials and products and observe prescribed process checks.
Enter measurements and compare recorded results with approved limits.
Assemble failed checks and supporting evidence for quality review.
Decide release, rework or further inspection for failed or ambiguous checks.

tasks.design: Configure the {OPS_SYSTEM} to select approved checklists, record observations and compare measurements with limits. A bounded document extractor checks evidence in {DOCS}, while a {WORKFLOW} assembles discrepancies for the quality supervisor's disposition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical observations, document checks and release decisions were mixed together. Specification revisions and evidence were difficult to connect reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned checklists, structured measurement forms and deterministic limit checks are established technology. Bounded extraction reduces document reading without replacing physical inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle defects, sampling adequacy and ambiguous specifications need trained judgement. Instrument integration and specialised inspection equipment may be expensive.
tasks.human_edge: People recognise unexpected physical conditions and decide when an apparently compliant result still needs investigation.

ambition.what: A daily review of repeated checklist failures by production stage.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time inspecting and investigating repeated failures, with less evidence assembly. They gain scope to propose targeted checks; release authority stays with the quality supervisor.

reach.task: Analyse repeated nonconformities and propose corrective actions.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, specification control and corrective-action evidence.

evidence.claim: Approved checklists and numeric tolerance checks can be configured without model judgement.
Document extraction can assist completeness checking, but does not establish physical conformity or justify release.

assumptions: The clerk performs prescribed checks within their training; specialist inspections remain with qualified roles.
Approved limits and specification revisions can be represented explicitly.
Observation entry remains partly manual; no machine-vision or instrument retrofit is included.
Build estimates include representative failed-check trials and GDPR review where evidence identifies employees.
unknowns: Which checks the clerk is qualified and authorised to perform.
Whether specification revisions are reliably linked to production orders.
Which measurements can be captured directly from instruments.
Whether sector-specific validation or national consultation requirements add rollout work.
research_questions: Which checks are objective field or tolerance checks, and which require interpretation?
Can unreadable evidence and incorrect specification revisions be reliably routed for review?
new_work: Review uncertain document extraction and retain source evidence.
Maintain approved checklists, tolerances and revision links.
Investigate false alerts and missed discrepancies during rollout.
Review recurring failures without turning process records into employee scoring.
tasks.statement: Examine documents, materials, or products and monitor work processes to assess completeness, accuracy, and conformance to standards and specifications.

tasks.short: Determine material and capacity requirements from work orders, schedules and staffing information.

steps.what: Retrieve current work orders, production schedules and staffing tables.
Read work-order attachments and approved notes for additional requirements.

loop.input: Approved work-order attachments and notes without structured requirement fields.
loop.output: Item quantities, setup needs, skill categories and due dates with source passages.
loop.check: Check revision, item identifiers, units and quantities against master data; confirm additions before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per attachment; unreadable, contradictory or unknown requirements go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use direct mappings for structured fields; varying free-text instructions need bounded interpretation.

steps.what: Calculate material quantities and capacity requirements across scheduled work.
Compare requirements with usable inventory, reservations and available capacity.
Confirm material priorities and resolve unusual capacity requirements with the supervisor.

tasks.design: Configure requirements calculation and availability checks in {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, using approved bills of materials and routing standards. Use a bounded loop only for unstructured attachments in {DOCS}, then show shortages and aggregate capacity gaps in {BI} for supervisor decisions on exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were split between master data, attachments and local calculations. Missing revisions and uncertain stock availability made automatic results hard to trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing requirements planning handles structured calculations. Cheaper integration development and source-linked extraction can cover the remaining document gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect bills of materials, quarantined stock, undocumented substitutions and unrealistic routing standards still produce misleading answers.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unusual setups and distinguish a genuine shortage from stock that is recorded but unusable.
tasks.altitude: The clerk investigates requirement exceptions and discusses readiness before each shift. With delegated limits, they can resolve approved master-data discrepancies; supervisors retain substitution and staffing decisions.

reach.task: Reconcile usable stock and reservations against production demand.
reach.learn: Learn stock status, lot restrictions and reservation rules.

reach.task: Determine whether held materials can enter production.
reach.learn: Learn release evidence, traceability requirements and why availability differs from physical quantity.

evidence.claim: Bills of materials, routing standards and availability rules support deterministic requirement calculations when master data is maintained.
Qargo documents extraction from PDF orders; applying extraction to manufacturing requirements still needs local validation.

assumptions: Requirements are mostly structured; attachments carry a smaller set of additional constraints.
This differs from the document-heavy prior because standard production orders commonly reference master data.
Staffing inputs use aggregate availability and skill categories where possible.
Outputs do not rank employees or allocate named people.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one site.
unknowns: How much requirement information exists only in attachments.
Whether bills of materials and routing standards match current production.
Whether stock statuses and reservations are reliable.
Whether aggregate staffing availability is sufficient.
Which access and consultation requirements apply under GDPR and national rules.
research_questions: Which requirement fields cause the most corrections today?
Can attachment requirements become structured fields at their source?
Which shortage rules already exist in the current planning configuration?
new_work: Review uncertain extractions and missing source revisions.
Correct master-data exceptions through the approved change process.
Maintain stock-status and capacity interpretation rules.
Check that aggregated staffing data remains sufficient and appropriately restricted.
tasks.statement: Review documents, such as production schedules, work orders, or staffing tables, to determine personnel or materials requirements or material priorities.

tasks.short: Review production progress with supervisors and agree necessary changes.

steps.what: Check completed work, work in progress, and missed milestones in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Prepare a progress brief in {DOCS} for the supervisor discussion.
Discuss actual progress, emerging problems, and practical constraints with supervisors.
Agree production changes, responsible people, and completion dates.
Enter agreed changes and actions in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: An exception view in the {OPS_SYSTEM} feeds a deterministic progress brief, replacing repeated document assembly. Supervisors and the clerk discuss constraints and approve structured changes; the {WORKFLOW} applies those changes and tracks action dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress data is often late, and the important explanation sits with supervisors. Preparing a common factual view takes time even when the discussion must remain human.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational reports and structured action forms can supply the meeting. Small generators and write-back connections are cheaper to build with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Supervisors must expose bad news and explain local constraints. A dashboard cannot establish whether reported progress is physically credible.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the question that reveals an unreported constraint and secure a realistic agreement across departments.

ambition.what: Same-shift review of newly blocked production work.

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to floor discussions and following through on difficult actions. The clerk can surface issues earlier; production approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess whether quality holds explain recurring production delays.
reach.learn: Hold reasons, release authority, traceability, and defect escalation.

evidence.claim: Progress dashboards, template briefs, structured approvals, and action tracking can be implemented without model reasoning.
The digest supplies no direct case demonstrating automation of production supervisor discussions.

assumptions: Production execution uses workflow 'other' because the supplied list has no production-execution workflow.
Preparation changes more than the conversation, consistent with the task's strong human-work prior.
Structured decisions are captured during approval; automatic meeting transcription is unnecessary.
External recovery uses the approved changes from this task rather than repeating the same decision.
GDPR and applicable national consultation rules govern any identifiable worker activity data.
Build ranges assume an existing production status feed and a limited department pilot.
unknowns: How quickly supervisors and operators record actual progress.
Which schedule changes supervisors may approve without escalation.
Whether action tracking already exists in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Employee consultation requirements for changed visibility of work activity.
research_questions: Which exception thresholds lead to useful discussions instead of alert fatigue?
Can the current system capture structured decisions during the existing meeting?
new_work: Correct stale progress and disputed exception flags.
Maintain milestone definitions and escalation thresholds.
Close actions and investigate repeated missed dates.
Check that dashboards support coordination rather than unsupported worker rankings.
tasks.statement: Confer with department supervisors or other personnel to assess progress and discuss needed changes.

tasks.short: Revise production schedules after disruptions and agree the resulting tradeoffs.

steps.what: Check shortages, backlog, capacity and current production progress.
Read engineering changes and interruption notes for scheduling implications.

loop.input: Approved engineering changes and interruption notes linked to work orders.
loop.output: Proposed dates, affected items, dependencies and constraints, each with a source passage.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, units, approval status and dates; the clerk confirms extracted constraints before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved or conflicting fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured changes use direct fields, but free-text notes contain constraints that fixed mappings miss.

steps.what: Calculate alternative sequences and their effects on completion dates.
Discuss feasible changes with production, engineering and sales.
Choose and approve a revised schedule within operational and commercial limits.
Enter the approved revision and release the updated production schedule.

tasks.design: Join current production and material data from {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, then run a deterministic scheduling solver on {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop turns free-text changes in {DOCS} into checked constraints, while {WORKFLOW} presents alternatives for discussion and approval before releasing the selected revision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local constraints were incomplete, and spreadsheet scenarios took too long to rebuild during interruptions. Several departments controlled different parts of the decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Established scheduling solvers and system interfaces already address the calculation. AI-assisted coding reduces connector work, while bounded extraction helps with approved free-text changes.
tasks.still_hard: Setup times, uncertain recovery dates and conflicting customer commitments can defeat an apparently feasible schedule. Agreement between departments remains necessary.
tasks.human_edge: Judge which promise to protect, negotiate scarce capacity and recognise operational constraints missing from the data.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time comparing recovery options with supervisors and less time rebuilding scenarios. Delegated limits could let them release small resequencing changes; production management retains decisions affecting major commitments or extra spending.

reach.task: Balance recovery options across material availability, capacity and customer commitments.
reach.learn: Learn constraint modelling, scenario sensitivity and the authority limits for changing commitments.

reach.task: Assess how production revisions affect dispatch capacity.
reach.learn: Learn transport cutoffs and how to distinguish forecast dates from confirmed promises.

evidence.claim: Constraint solvers can calculate production alternatives; local feasibility and commercial tradeoffs still require validation.
Qargo documents PDF order extraction, supporting bounded document intake as an existing capability, not production constraint interpretation.
The EU AI Act identifies certain employment-related allocation and monitoring uses; scope depends on the actual scheduling design.

assumptions: The initial scope schedules work orders and aggregate capacity, without scoring individual workers.
A solver first uses existing planning capability where it can express the required constraints.
Every released revision refers to the exact approved scenario and data snapshot.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one site, not measured savings.
GDPR applies to employee data; national rules determine consultation requirements. Consultation lead times can exceed the estimate.
unknowns: Whether existing planning configuration can represent setup, material and capacity constraints.
Which decisions the clerk can make without management approval.
Whether staffing data contains identifiable employee information.
Whether the intended allocation or monitoring features fall within EU AI Act employment provisions.
Which employee consultation and working-time requirements apply under national rules.
research_questions: Which historical disruptions expose missing constraints in the current schedule?
Can the current planning configuration solve representative cases before commissioning a separate solver?
Which changes require commercial approval as well as production approval?
new_work: Maintain setup times, priorities and solver constraints.
Review extracted constraints and resolve conflicting source notes.
Investigate infeasible scenarios and stale production events.
Monitor scenario stability so frequent recalculation does not cause constant resequencing.
Maintain approval limits, access controls and the applicable consultation arrangements.
tasks.statement: Revise production schedules when required due to design changes, labor or material shortages, backlogs, or other interruptions, collaborating with management, marketing, sales, production, or engineering.

tasks.short: Coordinate production and shipping recovery with colleagues, suppliers, and customers.

steps.what: Check affected orders, production progress, and shipment dates in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Read delay messages in {EMAIL} and identify causes and missing information.

loop.input: Delay messages and affected order identifiers.
loop.output: Cited causes, proposed dates, unresolved questions, and affected orders.
loop.check: Validate order identifiers and dates; show source passages; clerk checks consequential claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per message; unresolved conflicts return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Messages describe causes and conditional dates in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Discuss practical recovery options with department supervisors.
Discuss delivery alternatives and complaints with suppliers or customers.
Approve consequential commitments and record the recovery plan in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Send approved dates and responsibilities through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure an exception view in the {OPS_SYSTEM}; a bounded reader turns relevant {EMAIL} messages into a cited delay brief. People negotiate recovery, while the {WORKFLOW} records commitment approval and sends template confirmations containing only approved facts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order status and explanations arrive separately; resolving conflicting interests cannot be reduced to status rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing event feeds and approval features handle the structured work. Bounded text extraction makes message preparation feasible, with AI coding reducing connector development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier promises may be unreliable. Customer concessions, scarce capacity, and competing commitments still require negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which promise will preserve trust and which recovery option colleagues can actually deliver.

ambition.what: Early recovery options for customers whose orders are at risk.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling status to preparing recovery choices and negotiating exceptions. Final commitment rights stay with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Compare split shipment and later shipment options.
reach.learn: Transport constraints, incremental freight cost, and delivery reliability.

evidence.claim: Status views, approval routing, and approved template notifications are established deterministic patterns.
A documented loading-slot case shows coordination benefits; it does not establish production complaint automation.
Order text can be extracted into structured fields; this supports extraction feasibility, not reliable negotiation.

assumptions: Typical work uses operational records alongside messages and calls; the mail share is a prior, not a measured baseline.
External discussion stays within delegated authority; changed commitments require the approval shown.
Confirmations use approved recipients and templates; free-text model drafts are never sent automatically.
GDPR applies to personal contact data; EU AI Act obligations depend on the deployed functions.
Build ranges are indicative working-day effort for a limited pilot, not proven delivery times.
unknowns: Available order identifiers, event feeds, and message access.
Who may approve delivery changes, concessions, and extra freight.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
Actual time spent preparing, negotiating, and confirming recovery.
research_questions: What extraction accuracy is achievable for conditional dates and conflicting messages?
Which operational events reliably predict a missed shipment?
new_work: Check extracted causes and conditional dates.
Resolve unmatched orders and contradictory promises.
Maintain approval limits, templates, recipient rules, and connectors.
tasks.statement: Confer with establishment personnel, vendors, or customers to coordinate production or shipping activities and to resolve complaints or eliminate delays.

tasks.short: Record production quantities, material consumption and quality measurements against production orders.

steps.what: Collect shift sheets containing output, material consumption and quality measurements.
Check order references, units and totals against production records.
Resolve missing counts, unexplained consumption or questionable measurements with the shift supervisor.
Enter validated quantities, consumption and measurements against the production order.
Approve quality measurements and record any required quality disposition.
Copy approved totals into a parallel production summary workbook.

tasks.design: Configure structured shift capture in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with order identifiers, unit checks and required fields. A deterministic connector records validated submissions and routes discrepancies to the clerk; quality disposition retains its approval gate. An existing {OPS_SYSTEM} report replaces the duplicate workbook.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper capture, inconsistent units and delayed corrections make automatic posting unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured entry and existing validation features remove most transcription. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting capture to production records.
tasks.still_hard: Software cannot establish whether a physical count or measurement was taken correctly. Scrap, rework and backdated corrections need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Find the physical cause of discrepancies and distinguish recording errors from genuine production or quality problems.

ambition.what: Within-shift review of abnormal material consumption

tasks.altitude: The clerk works from a discrepancy queue instead of entering shift totals. They can gain authority to request an immediate consumption check; quality disposition remains with the quality lead.

reach.task: Investigate recurring gaps between material consumption, good output and scrap.
reach.learn: Measurement traceability, yield calculations and quality disposition codes.

evidence.claim: Structured production capture, unit validation and duplicate-safe posting can use deterministic software.
The digest provides no documented manufacturing production-recording case for this proposed design.

assumptions: The baseline represents a plant using paper shift sheets alongside the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Operators enter measurements at source; this creates operator capture work and requires rollout support.
Duplicate workbook removal assumes an existing report meets its users' needs.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for one site.
GDPR applies to identifiable operator records. National rules may require consultation over changed work practices or monitoring.
unknowns: Are shift measurements already captured digitally?
Which fields affect stock valuation, payroll or regulated quality records?
Does the {OPS_SYSTEM} support corrections with an audit history?
Which consultation and device-access requirements apply?
research_questions: Can native capture forms and interfaces cover the required production fields?
How should duplicate submissions, late entries and reversals be tested against inventory balances?
new_work: Operators capture structured shift data at source.
Review validation failures and unexplained consumption.
Maintain units, material mappings and tolerance rules.
Reconcile connector failures and audit corrections.
tasks.statement: Record production data, including volume produced, consumption of raw materials, or quality control measures.

tasks.short: Maintain material availability and raise replenishment requests for production.

steps.what: Retrieve stock, reservations, and expected receipts from the {ERP}.
Run material requirements calculations against the production schedule in the {ERP}.
Investigate suspect stock balances with warehouse staff and physical checks.
Authorise inventory corrections in the {ERP}.
Select replenishment quantities and dates, considering shortages and approved supply options.
Enter the purchase requisition in {PROCUREMENT}.
Approve the purchase requisition for the purchasing team.

tasks.design: Configure material requirements and exception rules in the {ERP}, with a traceable inventory correction flow. A deterministic link creates requisitions in {PROCUREMENT}; existing approval rules govern release to purchasing, while people investigate physical discrepancies and unusual supply choices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inaccurate stock, lead times, and bills of materials make automatic proposals unreliable. Clerks bridge gaps between planning and purchasing records.
tasks.enabler_now: Material planning and requisition approvals already exist in standard systems. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and adding validation; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Physical stock errors, supplier unreliability, minimum quantities, and unapproved substitutes cannot be solved by cleaner calculations alone.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real shortage from bad records and recognise when a substitute needs technical approval.

ambition.what: Daily review of materials likely to stop production.

tasks.altitude: The week centres on material risks and inventory causes instead of requisition entry. Spending and substitution approval rights remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Propose safety-stock and lead-time changes for recurring shortages.
reach.learn: Demand variability, service targets, inventory cost, and supplier performance.

reach.task: Investigate recurring stock discrepancies.
reach.learn: Receipt timing, stock movements, count controls, and unit conversions.

evidence.claim: Material requirements calculations, replenishment parameters, and requisition approvals are established system capabilities.
Integrated warehouse and transport records are commercially available; this does not prove manufacturing replenishment outcomes.

assumptions: The company has repeatable material demand and maintained bills of materials.
Routine receipt booking belongs to warehouse operations; this task handles availability and discrepancies.
Purchase order placement follows requisition approval and remains a purchasing task.
Personal data remains access-controlled under GDPR; employee monitoring changes require assessment under national rules.
Build ranges cover a pilot material group and exclude a full inventory data cleanup.
unknowns: Availability and licensing of existing material planning features.
Accuracy of stock, bills of materials, units, and replenishment parameters.
Whether {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} share records or need a connector.
Inventory adjustment, substitution, and purchasing approval limits.
research_questions: Which parameter errors most often produce false shortages?
Can existing system configuration remove requisition re-entry without custom code?
new_work: Investigate rejected or duplicate requisitions.
Maintain lead times, minimum quantities, units, and supplier mappings.
Review false shortages and repeated inventory adjustments.
Monitor connector failures and approval queues.
tasks.statement: Requisition and maintain inventories of materials or supplies necessary to meet production demands.

tasks.short: Calculate production material, labour, manufacturing cost and wage estimates from approved rates.

steps.what: Retrieve quantities, bills of materials, routing times and approved cost rates.
Select batch size, expected scrap and working-time assumptions for the estimate.
Calculate material quantities, labour hours, manufacturing costs and wage estimates.
Check units, effective rates and unusual variances against prior estimates.
Approve the estimate before it supports resource or overtime commitments.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} costing and requirements functions to use versioned bills of materials, routings and effective rate tables from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}. Explicit assumptions produce reproducible estimates and variance flags, with supervisor approval before resource commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Arithmetic was already automated in many companies, but copied rates, stale routings and local spreadsheet assumptions caused repeated checking.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calculation engines can cover the arithmetic. AI coding makes small input adapters and validation rules cheaper to build; no model is needed for calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Scrap, setup time, overtime eligibility and unusual production conditions remain uncertain. Standard software may already do most of the task, limiting additional savings.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk understands when standard rates and production assumptions do not represent the actual job.

ambition.what: A same-day overtime-versus-rescheduling cost comparison for threatened production orders.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time checking arithmetic and more time testing operational assumptions. They can propose costed alternatives; budget, overtime and payroll approval rights do not expand.

reach.task: Compare production batch sizes and timing against material and labour constraints.
reach.learn: Scenario analysis, cost drivers and sensitivity to uncertain assumptions.

evidence.claim: Material requirements and standard production costs can be calculated deterministically from quantities, routings and approved rates.
Where existing software already performs the arithmetic, the main remaining gain comes from input quality and reduced reconciliation.

assumptions: The {ERP} includes configurable requirements and costing functions; this must be checked before building anything.
Wage outputs are planning estimates using approved rates, not payslips or payroll instructions.
The initial implementation uses standard labour rates rather than identifiable employee pay.
Build estimates include rate-version testing, access review and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: How much calculation and validation the customer's {ERP} already performs.
Whether bills of materials, routing times and rate effective dates are maintained reliably.
Which wage rules, premiums and rounding conventions apply.
Whether individual pay data or changes to working-time rules are in scope.
research_questions: Can configuration remove the local calculation workbook?
Which historical orders reveal unit, rate-version and rounding errors?
Which assumptions materially change the overtime-versus-rescheduling comparison?
new_work: Maintain rate effective dates, units and approved calculation rules.
Review unusual variances and stale routing assumptions.
Reconcile configuration changes against representative historical calculations.
tasks.statement: Calculate figures, such as required amounts of labor or materials, manufacturing costs, or wages, using pricing schedules, adding machines, calculators, or computers.

tasks.short: Distribute released production schedules and work orders, then resolve missing acknowledgements.

steps.what: Retrieve the released production schedule and associated work orders.
Check schedule versions, department assignments and release status.
Prepare separate schedule documents for each department.
Send schedule packets and highlight changes to department supervisors.
Chase missing acknowledgements and resolve access or routing problems.

tasks.design: Configure release events in the {OPS_SYSTEM} to publish department views and revision differences through {WORKFLOW}. Send links through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}, track acknowledgements and route overdue or failed deliveries to the clerk; generate controlled printouts only where needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Department copies drifted from the released schedule. Routing lists and acknowledgements lived outside the production record.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing release events, permissions and notification rules can handle most distribution. AI-assisted coding makes missing connectors and revision comparisons cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Shared terminals, offline workstations and obsolete printed copies still need practical controls.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an acknowledgement hides a misunderstanding about what the department must actually change.
tasks.altitude: The clerk checks distribution exceptions instead of assembling daily packets. With delegated authority, they can correct routing and access within agreed limits; production priorities remain with production management.

reach.task: Prepare dispatch work from the latest released production schedule.
reach.learn: Understand dispatch cutoffs, order identifiers and which schedule changes affect loading.

evidence.claim: Release-triggered routing, revision comparison and acknowledgement reminders can use configured workflows without a model.
Boltrics provides operational records across warehouse and transport functions; this does not establish production schedule distribution capability.

assumptions: A released schedule has a stable identifier and revision.
Digital department views can replace most separately prepared packets.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Production execution uses order-to-cash because the workflow list has no production-specific stream.
Build ranges assume one site and existing system licences.
unknowns: Whether release events, department permissions and acknowledgement features are available.
Which departments require controlled paper copies.
Who may change routing and distribution rules.
Whether acknowledgement logging requires employee consultation under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Can existing release subscriptions meet the need before building a connector?
What evidence distinguishes delivery, acknowledgement and operational acceptance?
new_work: Resolve failed deliveries and incorrect access.
Maintain department routing and escalation rules.
Check that obsolete printed schedules are withdrawn.
Apply GDPR access and retention controls where acknowledgement records identify employees.
tasks.statement: Distribute production schedules or work orders to departments.

tasks.short: Gather production, inventory and customer information for status reporting.

steps.what: Retrieve production progress, stock balances and order details.
Read shift sheets and supervisor messages for updates missing from system records.

loop.input: Shift sheets and supervisor updates with known production order identifiers.
loop.output: Proposed quantities, completion times and shortage notes with source references.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, units, timestamps and quantity bounds; clerk accepts proposed entries.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per document; unresolved fields enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Some updates contain free text and inconsistent layouts; structured updates bypass the model.

steps.what: Copy source figures into a consolidated workbook and align order identifiers.
Clarify missing quantities, conflicting dates and unexplained inventory differences with supervisors.
Apply confirmed corrections and prepare the reporting dataset.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} join records from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}, replacing the consolidation workbook. A bounded extractor proposes updates from {DOCS} and {EMAIL} for clerk acceptance; validation rules flag gaps and feed a timestamped {BI} view.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order identifiers, update times and units differed between sources. Informal shift updates required someone to interpret and chase them.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces, scheduled imports and validation rules handle structured records. AI coding reduces implementation effort, while bounded extraction can handle irregular notes.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded shop-floor activity and disputed stock figures still require investigation. Faster refreshes cannot repair missing source events.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows which discrepancy signals a real production problem and whom to ask for a reliable correction.

ambition.what: A shift-level shortage watch for small production cells without dedicated planners.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less of the week assembling figures and more time resolving material and progress discrepancies. They can prioritise investigations; production commitments remain with supervisors.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of late production completion.
reach.learn: Event timestamps, inventory reconciliation and basic cause analysis.

evidence.claim: Scheduled joins, validation rules and dashboards can replace recurring compilation of structured production records.
Qargo's FCE Transport case demonstrates extraction of order information from PDFs; this is adjacent evidence, not a production-reporting case.

assumptions: The company uses an {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}, with a workbook bridging their reporting outputs.
The target covers production and material status rather than individual employee performance.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Access work includes GDPR checks where records contain personal data and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether order identifiers and units agree across the customer's systems.
Which interfaces, exports and reporting permissions are available.
How often shift updates arrive outside system records.
Whether employee-level monitoring or national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration supply the joined dataset without a new integration?
Which validation rules distinguish late data from genuine production exceptions?
new_work: Review extracted updates and investigate unresolved discrepancies.
Maintain identifier mappings, unit conversions and freshness thresholds.
Monitor failed imports and source-record coverage.
tasks.statement: Compile information, such as production rates and progress, materials inventories, materials used, or customer information, so that status reports can be completed.

tasks.short: Arrange parts delivery and internal handling to keep production moving.

steps.what: Check shortages, part locations and required delivery times.
Request current availability and delivery promises from existing suppliers.
Negotiate practical delivery or assembly arrangements with suppliers and department supervisors.
Approve premium freight or other commitments outside the clerk's authority.
Book the agreed delivery and confirm the collection or arrival slot.
Create internal movement or assembly orders against the released production schedule.
Agree safe handling and assembly sequence with the warehouse and production teams.
Verify delivered parts against the delivery booking and movement order.
Record receipt and update the expedite status for production planning.

tasks.design: Connect shortages in {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} to an expedite record in {WORKFLOW}, with standard availability enquiries through {EMAIL}. Prepare bookings through {PARTNER_PORTAL} for clerk approval, generate internal orders from approved arrangements and update status from confirmed receipt events.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier promises, bookings and internal handling instructions were disconnected. Staff had to chase each handoff without a shared exception record.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured enquiries, approval rules and event links can remove much of the chase. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of supplier mappings and duplicate-booking checks; no model is needed for the proposed core flow.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier promises can change, some portals lack interfaces, and physical handling depends on local capacity and safe working arrangements.
tasks.human_edge: Secure credible commitments, negotiate recovery options and coordinate people when the planned movement cannot happen.
tasks.altitude: The clerk concentrates on threatened commitments and recovery conversations. Delegated spending and booking limits could let them complete routine expedites independently; exceptional costs remain with the supply chain manager.

reach.task: Coordinate inbound receipts and internal movements against production priorities.
reach.learn: Learn receiving capacity, stock accuracy and safe material handoff requirements.

reach.task: Compare recovery transport options for production-critical parts.
reach.learn: Learn transport constraints, premium freight economics and how to verify a delivery promise.

evidence.claim: Standard enquiries, spending checks, booking validation and receipt-driven updates can use deterministic workflows.
A Smurfit Kappa plant case reports reduced truck turnaround after time-slot management; it supports delivery coordination, not end-to-end parts expediting.
Boltrics provides warehouse and transport records that can support connected material movements.

assumptions: The steps describe a supplier-linked expedite; internal-only cases skip supplier enquiries and external booking.
Standard enquiries request information without changing orders, prices or commitments.
Manager approval is conditional on spending or commitment thresholds.
Automated internal orders use approved work instructions and released production priorities.
Physical verification remains with receiving staff; automation records their confirmed result.
Time shares cover the participating roles in this task and are estimates, not a measured clerk-only time study.
unknowns: Which suppliers support structured promises and booking interfaces.
Which purchases and bookings fall within the clerk's authority.
How receipt confirmations reach the operational systems.
Which assembly activities need separate technical or quality approval.
Whether changed tracking or working arrangements require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which supplier interfaces cover the largest share of expedite cases?
What checks prevent duplicate bookings after a timeout or changed promise?
Which internal handoffs fail despite a confirmed external delivery?
new_work: Resolve missing or conflicting supplier promises.
Maintain supplier mappings, spending limits and enquiry templates.
Review external bookings before commitment.
Investigate delivery discrepancies and failed receipt updates.
Maintain access and GDPR retention controls for supplier and employee contact records.
tasks.statement: Arrange for delivery, assembly, or distribution of supplies or parts to expedite flow of materials and meet production schedules.

tasks.short: Confirm supplier shipment quantities, dates and references, then resolve discrepancies and update production planning.

steps.what: Identify shipments needing confirmation against purchase orders and production requirements.
Ask suppliers to confirm dispatch dates, quantities and shipment references.
Check supplier confirmations against purchase order quantities and required delivery dates.

loop.input: Supplier confirmation text and attachments, with purchase order references.
loop.output: Proposed shipment fields, source excerpts and missing-field flags.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, units and dates against the purchase order; clerk approves accepted fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per confirmation; unresolved fields enter the clerk's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier prose and attachment layouts vary. Structured portal responses bypass the model.

steps.what: Discuss missing details or delays and agree escalation with the supplier.
Record confirmed shipment details and notify production planning of material changes.

tasks.design: Configure a confirmation queue in the {PROCUREMENT} and send approved factual requests through the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded extractor proposes fields from supplier replies; clerk-approved details update the {OPS_SYSTEM} and trigger planning notifications. Supplier calls remain human, supported by a concise discrepancy brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier replies lack consistent fields, and purchase orders and production dates sit in separate systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing request templates and field validation handle routine work. AI-assisted coding makes the connector cheaper; bounded extraction handles varied replies.
tasks.still_hard: A promised date may be unreliable. Recovering from shortages requires supplier trust and production trade-offs.
tasks.human_edge: Judge supplier credibility, uncover unstated delays and negotiate recovery without making unauthorised commitments.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time chasing routine confirmations and more time resolving credible shortage risks. They can gain authority to trigger a shortage review; purchasing commitments remain with the purchasing role.

reach.task: Assess which late inbound shipments threaten the next production shift.
reach.learn: Lead-time variability, shipment milestones and material criticality.

evidence.claim: Qargo extracts PDF orders into fields. This supports the extraction pattern, not shipment-confirmation accuracy.
Queues, templated requests and approved field updates can use deterministic workflow rules.

assumptions: Scope is one site's inbound shipments with stable purchase order identifiers.
Automatic requests only ask for facts; they do not change orders or accept revised commercial terms.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
GDPR applies to supplier contact data. Access work includes applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which suppliers provide structured confirmations or portal access?
Can shipment fields be written through supported interfaces?
Who may accept revised delivery dates or escalate shortages?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing confirmation features remove the need for a custom connector?
Which date and quantity checks catch ambiguous supplier replies before acceptance?
new_work: Review extracted shipment fields and resolve unmatched references.
Maintain request templates, reminder limits and contact records.
Monitor failed updates and reconcile duplicate supplier replies.
tasks.statement: Contact suppliers to verify shipment details.

tasks.short: File operational documents, link them to records and keep them complete, retrievable and correctly retained.

steps.what: Collect maintenance records, bills of lading and cost reports from departmental mailboxes.
Check document completeness and match documents to shipments, assets or production orders.

loop.input: Unstructured operational documents and permitted reference records.
loop.output: Proposed document type, identifiers and record links, with source excerpts.
loop.check: Validate identifiers against reference records; clerk approves inferred links. Exact structured matches bypass review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; ambiguous links remain unfiled in an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Some documents lack consistent metadata or layouts. Existing identifiers are matched deterministically first.

steps.what: Scan paper originals using a scanner and check page completeness.
Name files, store documents and update links in the operational records.
Request missing documents from departmental owners.
Approve retention or disposal after checking retention periods and legal holds.

tasks.design: Connect designated {EMAIL} folders and operational exports to a controlled register in the {DOCS}. Deterministic rules handle known references, naming and reminders; a bounded extractor proposes metadata for irregular documents, with clerk approval of inferred links. Retention rules produce a disposal preview, checked against legal holds and approved before deletion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents arrive through separate channels with weak identifiers. Retention decisions and legal holds are not consistently connected to filing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing metadata, versioning and retention features cover much of the register. AI-assisted coding lowers connector effort, and bounded extraction helps with irregular documents.
tasks.still_hard: Paper originals, missing signatures, disputed versions and legally required retention need explicit handling.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a document is incomplete, unreliable or subject to a dispute, and secure the authoritative record.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time naming and moving files and more time resolving evidence gaps. They can gain authority to assemble audit packets; disposal approval remains with the records manager.

reach.task: Reconcile delivery evidence with shipment and receipt records.
reach.learn: Shipment identifiers, proof-of-delivery requirements and document provenance.

reach.task: Check that asset maintenance evidence is complete before an inspection.
reach.learn: Asset registers, maintenance intervals and required inspection records.

evidence.claim: Qargo with TransFollow creates and signs electronic consignment notes inside a transport system.
The digest notes that paper consignment notes may still be needed abroad; paper handling cannot universally disappear.
Metadata registers, controlled access, retention previews and duplicate detection can use existing document features and deterministic rules.

assumptions: The initial scope covers selected document classes at one site.
Source-generated digital documents reduce scanning; remaining paper originals still receive completeness checks.
Deletion requires approval and a current legal hold check.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to personal data in documents. Retention periods and employee consultation depend partly on national rules.
unknowns: Which document classes require paper originals or specific retention periods?
Where are legal holds recorded, and who approves disposal?
How many documents lack reliable order, shipment or asset identifiers?
Which mailboxes and record stores may the connector access?
research_questions: Can native document metadata and retention features cover the initial scope?
Which matching thresholds prevent documents being linked to the wrong order?
How should missing pages, superseded versions and duplicate scans be detected?
new_work: Review uncertain document links and incomplete scans.
Maintain document classes, retention schedules and access groups.
Approve disposal previews and reconcile legal holds.
Monitor connector failures and audit document provenance.
tasks.statement: Maintain files, such as maintenance records, bills of lading, or cost reports.

tasks.short: Turn sales forecasts into feasible production commitments and timetables.

steps.what: Retrieve the approved sales forecast from the {ERP}.
Collect open orders, material availability, and routing times from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Collect supervisor confirmations of capacity limits and planned downtime through {EMAIL}.
Build a base production timetable in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Compare alternative sequences and commitment dates in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Review trade-offs and select a proposed timetable with supervisors.
Approve production commitments and the timetable in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Publish the approved timetable to departments through the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Connect forecast data from the {ERP} and constraints from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using the existing planning module for the base timetable. A deterministic solver on the {DATA_PLATFORM} compares bounded scenarios and validates capacity, materials, and frozen periods; the {WORKFLOW} captures approval before publication to the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forecasts, capacity calendars, and material constraints are inconsistently aligned. Spreadsheet scenarios are difficult to maintain when priorities or assumptions change.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning modules handle the base calculation, while deterministic solvers handle explicit constraints. AI coding lowers the cost of connecting data and building scenario comparisons without requiring model judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Forecast error, uncertain process times, and conflicting service priorities remain. Moving from machine capacity to person-level allocation requires a separate EU AI Act assessment and consideration of national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which commitments deserve protection when a mathematically feasible plan would create an unacceptable commercial or operational outcome.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding timetables to comparing explicit trade-offs and challenging assumptions. The clerk gains faster scenario preparation; final commitment and resource approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Compare the cost and service effects of alternative capacity plans.
reach.learn: Constraint modelling, sensitivity analysis, and the difference between forecast error and execution failure.

reach.task: Prepare demand-and-capacity choices for cross-functional planning.
reach.learn: Planning horizons, frozen periods, inventory exposure, and commitment policy.

evidence.claim: Production planning modules and deterministic constraint solvers can generate and compare schedules without language models.
Feasibility requires explicit constraints and validation; the digest provides no measured production scheduling implementation case.

assumptions: The existing planning module can generate a base timetable; missing capability would change the estimate.
The solver schedules orders, machines, and aggregate capacity, not workers by behaviour or personal traits.
Scenario runs have fixed horizons, time limits, and constraints; infeasibility returns a conflict report.
Validation checks material timing, precedence, capacity, frozen periods, and differences from the approved schedule.
Supervisors confirm capacity through structured forms, replacing repeated mailbox chasing.
GDPR applies wherever personal data is processed; national rules may require consultation for working-time or monitoring changes.
Build ranges cover one bounded production area and exclude extensive master-data repair.
unknowns: Existing planning module capabilities, licences, and interfaces.
Quality of routing times, changeover rules, capacity calendars, and material availability.
Planning horizon, frozen periods, objective priorities, and acceptable solve time.
Whether proposed changes affect individual working times or employee monitoring.
Required access approvals and employee consultation processes.
research_questions: Can existing planning configuration generate useful scenarios before a separate solver is justified?
Which constraints explain the largest gap between planned and actual completion?
How do scenario results change when forecast and process-time assumptions vary?
new_work: Maintain constraint definitions, priorities, and planning parameters.
Investigate infeasible scenarios and stale capacity confirmations.
Compare approved schedules with execution and adjust unreliable assumptions.
Monitor solver time limits, interface failures, and schedule version conflicts.
tasks.statement: Plan production commitments or timetables for business units, specific programs, or jobs, using sales forecasts.

tasks.short: Prepare approved production directions, resource requirements, work locations and cost projections.

steps.what: Retrieve approved specifications, drawings and previous work instructions.
Calculate materials, tools, equipment, labour requirements and projected costs.
Confirm work locations, practical sequencing and resource availability with production supervisors.
Assemble construction directions, work locations, resource lists and cost projections into a draft pack.

loop.input: Approved source instructions, calculated requirements and confirmed feasibility notes.
loop.output: Draft explanatory directions with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Lock calculated tables; compare instruction references and flag unsupported directions for engineering review.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pack; missing or conflicting instructions go to the engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative instructions vary across products. Fixed tables and established instruction templates remain deterministic.

steps.what: Validate technical directions and approve the work pack for production use.
Attach the approved work pack to production orders and notify supervisors.

tasks.design: A generator combines approved revisions from the {DOCS}, resource data from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and cost rates from the {ERP}. Deterministic calculations produce resource and cost tables; a bounded drafting loop assembles source-linked narrative directions. Engineering approval releases the versioned pack to the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications, routing data and cost rates are fragmented. Practical production knowledge is often held by supervisors.
tasks.enabler_now: Version-controlled sources and reusable calculation templates already support much of the work. AI-assisted coding and bounded drafting reduce assembly effort.
tasks.still_hard: New production methods, safety-critical directions and realistic labour estimates require engineering knowledge and physical validation.
tasks.human_edge: Spot instructions that are technically plausible but impractical on the shop floor, and reconcile competing resource constraints.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time checking build readiness with supervisors and less time assembling documents. They can gain authority to request a readiness review; engineering retains approval of construction directions.

reach.task: Prepare the resource readiness checkpoint for a prototype build.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, change control and resource estimates.

evidence.claim: Approved bills of materials, routings and rates support deterministic resource and cost calculations.
Source-linked drafting can assist document assembly but does not establish technical correctness.

assumptions: The clerk prepares documentation from approved engineering inputs rather than designing manufacturing methods.
The first release covers one product family and its existing instruction templates.
Headcount estimates use approved labour standards, not predictions about individual workers.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies where records identify workers. Changes to working-time arrangements may require consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Are bills of materials, routings and drawings version-controlled and mutually consistent?
Who approves technical directions, cost assumptions and labour standards?
Which instructions require formal safety or regulatory validation?
Can approved packs be attached to production orders through supported interfaces?
research_questions: How much narrative assembly can existing templates eliminate?
Which checks detect obsolete revisions and unsupported construction directions?
new_work: Review generated narrative and resolve source conflicts.
Maintain templates, calculation rules and approved source mappings.
Test revision handling and withdraw superseded packs.
Compare projected requirements with actual build results.
tasks.statement: Establish and prepare product construction directions and locations and information on required tools, materials, equipment, numbers of workers needed, and cost projections.

tasks.short: Prepare production, transport, staffing, purchasing and maintenance documentation.

steps.what: Retrieve production sequences, shipment requirements and planned dates.
Obtain the approved staffing schedule and relevant availability.
Retrieve approved purchase orders and expected material delivery dates.
Retrieve maintenance and repair orders affecting equipment availability.
Populate templates and reconcile references across the preparation pack.
Review readiness conflicts and approve the pack for issue.
Issue approved documents to departments and archive the released version.

tasks.design: A template generator joins approved records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and a restricted {HCM} extract into versioned packs in {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} highlights missing references and readiness conflicts, obtains supervisor approval and distributes the released version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates used separate copies of changing source records. Cross-system references and release versions depended on manual checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic templates, record links and approval flows can be assembled with existing interfaces. AI coding reduces the effort of mapping fields and testing document variants.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting delivery, maintenance and staffing plans need operational decisions. Issued paper copies and late changes can still leave departments using obsolete instructions.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor judges whether a pack represents a workable and safe plan when resources conflict.

ambition.what: A pre-shift readiness pack showing material, equipment and approved staffing gaps.

tasks.altitude: The clerk shifts from document assembly to preparing readiness exceptions before the shift starts. They can coordinate corrections across departments; purchasing, staffing and production approvals remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Coordinate readiness dependencies for a production changeover.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, change control and escalation timing.

evidence.claim: TransFollow and Qargo support creating and signing transport documents inside an operational system; this supports the transport-document component.
Structured source records can populate production and maintenance templates through deterministic generation.
Employee scheduling and monitoring require separate assessment from simple document preparation under the EU AI Act.

assumptions: Document variants share stable order, equipment and revision identifiers.
The staffing extract contains only approved assignments and necessary availability, excluding absence reasons.
The solution reproduces approved staffing plans; it does not allocate employees using inferred traits.
Access estimates include GDPR controls and consultation under national rules where applicable; changed working-time rules may extend them.
unknowns: Which document variants and internal approval rules the customer uses.
Whether staffing and maintenance records expose suitable interfaces.
Whether paper documents are operationally required.
Which employee consultation requirements and access restrictions apply.
research_questions: Which templates can be replaced by existing document-generation configuration?
How should revised packs invalidate previously issued copies?
Can readiness gaps be detected using explicit rules before supervisor review?
new_work: Maintain templates, field mappings and document revision rules.
Resolve missing references and conflicting source dates.
Check distribution failures and obsolete-copy handling.
Review staffing-data access and retention.
tasks.statement: Compile and prepare documentation related to production sequences, transportation, personnel schedules, or purchase, maintenance, or repair orders.

tasks.short: Explain production delays, difficulties and cost estimate changes with supporting records.

steps.what: Retrieve production progress, material availability and cost records.
Collect messages explaining shortages, breakdowns and revised delivery dates.

loop.input: Messages linked to the work order.
loop.output: Dated disruption evidence with source references and unresolved claims.
loop.check: Validate order identifiers and dates; the clerk checks ambiguous causes and conflicting messages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per case; unresolved fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Messages describe causes and revised dates in varied free text.

steps.what: Ask the department supervisor to clarify causes, recovery actions and missing facts.
Compare original and revised costs and calculate the documented variance.
Write the explanation and attach supporting records.

loop.input: Confirmed explanation, calculated variance and linked evidence.
loop.output: A delay report separating confirmed facts, estimates and open questions.
loop.check: Copy numbers from validated calculations; require evidence references and clerk review of causal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported explanations remain blank for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles structure, but varied evidence needs a short written explanation.

steps.what: Approve material explanations, revised estimates and report release.
File the approved report and evidence against the work order.
Send the approved explanation to the designated recipients.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins work-order records from the {OPS_SYSTEM} with estimates and costs from the {ERP}, calculates variances and assembles evidence. Two bounded loops extract relevant messages from the {EMAIL} and {CHAT} and draft a report in the {DOCS}; the clerk checks evidence and discusses unresolved causes with the department supervisor. The {WORKFLOW} records manager approval, archives the approved version and releases it through the {EMAIL} using that same approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order identifiers, estimate versions and explanations sit in separate records and messages. Joining them was costly, while cause attribution still needed discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Available exports or APIs support deterministic joins and calculations. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort, and bounded extraction and drafting can handle variable text without deciding responsibility.
tasks.still_hard: Late production updates, missing cost allocations and disputed causes remain difficult. GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on use, especially if the scope expands to evaluating workers. Employee consultation and approval requirements follow national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk tests explanations against practical production knowledge and asks questions people may hesitate to answer in writing. The manager judges responsibility, commercial wording and whether a revised estimate is justified.

ambition.what: Weekly review of recurring delay causes and prevention priorities

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time collecting attachments and writing reports, and more time investigating recurring disruptions. They can gain delegated authority to request missing evidence and trigger agreed escalation thresholds; estimate approval remains with the manager.

reach.task: Compare material arrival delays with production disruptions.
reach.learn: Event timestamps, lead-time variation and the difference between correlation and cause.

reach.task: Assess whether a proposed process change reduces recurring delay costs.
reach.learn: Cost allocation, baseline selection and measuring results after a change.

evidence.claim: Production clerks commonly combine operational records, supervisor explanations and cost comparisons to document disruptions.
Record joins, version comparisons, variance calculations and approval routing can use deterministic technology.
Qargo reads PDF transport orders into fields; this supports bounded extraction feasibility, not automated production-cause attribution.
The EU AI Act distinguishes worker-related employment uses from ordinary operational document processing.
The Netherlands has works-council consent rules covering certain working-time and employee-monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: This is a typical mid-size production business with separate operational and financial records.
A spreadsheet bridges cost records and estimates; some companies already perform this comparison inside the {ERP}.
Material reports receive manager approval; routine factual updates may have delegated release rules.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
The prior's document-heavy pattern fits, but structured joins and calculations cover more work than its low rule-coverage estimate suggests.
The consultation range assumes a limited reporting change; formal national procedures can take longer.
The initial scope documents work orders and disruptions without scoring individual employees.
unknowns: Whether the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} share stable work-order identifiers.
Whether original estimates and revisions are retained with timestamps.
Which causes are already recorded in structured fields.
Who approves cost changes and customer-facing explanations.
Which APIs, exports and mailbox permissions are available.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules or agreements.
Actual case volumes, handling times and evidence retention requirements.
research_questions: How often can historical reports be reconstructed from existing records without another supervisor conversation?
Which variance components reconcile reliably to the {ERP}?
Can message extraction preserve contradictory evidence and identify unsupported causal claims?
Which existing {WORKFLOW} and {DOCS} features cover approval, version locking and filing?
new_work: Review ambiguous message extraction and unsupported report claims.
Resolve unmatched work orders, stale records and missing estimate versions.
Maintain variance formulas, evidence mappings and recipient rules.
Check failed imports and releases and preserve approval records.
Review access, retention and any changes affecting employee consultation.
tasks.statement: Provide documentation and information to account for delays, difficulties, or changes to cost estimates.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from copying schedules and chasing status toward preparing recovery choices and resolving exceptions across departments. Greater decision rights depend on explicit delegation for resequencing, bookings and spending.
reach: Support supply chain managers with costed disruption scenarios.
Work with inventory clerks on usable stock and reservation accuracy.
Help logistics analysts connect production changes to dispatch constraints.
Work with quality control managers on held-material readiness.
skills_to_grow: Model material, setup and capacity constraints.
Read scenario tradeoffs and test sensitivity to uncertain inputs.
Maintain master-data quality and traceable revisions.
Negotiate credible recovery commitments.
Understand approval limits, GDPR and applicable national consultation rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a short-horizon production readiness and recovery service that connects material availability, feasible schedules and delivery commitments, with delegated authority for small operational changes.

role_batches.altitude: The role moves toward production exception coordination and preparation of defensible recovery choices. People retain negotiations, physical verification, and commitment approval; shared data feeds and approval records prevent duplicate preparation across tasks.
reach: Support logistics analysts with recovery comparisons.
Support supply chain managers with material-risk and capacity scenarios.
Work with quality control systems managers on delays caused by quality holds.
Support management analysts with evidence on recurring planning constraints.
skills_to_grow: Material planning parameters and inventory controls.
Constraint-based scheduling and scenario interpretation.
Data quality diagnosis and operational event definitions.
Negotiation, escalation, and commitment management.
Approval configuration and integration exception handling.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a daily production-risk service that connects material shortages, blocked work, and threatened deliveries to feasible recovery choices for authorised decision-makers.

role_batches.altitude: The role moves from copying records and preparing documents toward resolving readiness gaps, testing assumptions and coordinating exceptions. Clerks gain scope to propose interventions, while quality release, staffing commitments and budget approval remain with authorised managers.
reach: Logistics analyst: investigate recurring production delays and compare resource scenarios.
Quality control systems manager: connect repeated inspection failures to corrective-action evidence.
Project management specialist: coordinate material, equipment and staffing dependencies for changeovers.
skills_to_grow: Data reconciliation, units and source-record traceability.
Configuration of templates, validation rules and exception queues.
Production costing and scenario analysis.
Specification control and inspection evidence.
Cross-department investigation and escalation.
GDPR-aware handling of employee and operational records.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A production readiness coordinator who provides timely material, equipment and staffing exception views, proposes costed recovery options and helps supervisors act before a shift loses output.

role_batches.altitude: The role moves toward material readiness, production discrepancy resolution and reliable operational evidence. Proposed decision rights cover initiating shortage and consumption reviews and assembling readiness or audit packs; purchasing, engineering, quality and disposal approvals stay with their accountable roles.
reach: Logistics analysis of inbound delays and production exposure.
Quality investigation of consumption, output and scrap discrepancies.
Project readiness checks for prototype builds.
skills_to_grow: Production order, material and shipment data relationships.
Unit validation, yield calculations and correction traceability.
Supplier escalation and practical production constraints.
Document revision control, retention and provenance.
Reviewing source-linked extraction and drafting outputs.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide shift-start material risk reviews, within-shift consumption alerts and engineering-approved prototype readiness packs from a shared operational record. Start with reusable templates and validation rules; connect live systems once the employer grants access.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward investigating disruption patterns and preparing prevention proposals. Broader escalation rights require explicit delegation; managerial cost and commercial decisions remain accountable human decisions.
reach: Logistics analysis of material delays affecting production.
Management analysis of recurring disruption costs and prevention results.
skills_to_grow: Operational data reconciliation
Cost variance interpretation
Evidence-based cause investigation
Clear explanations of uncertainty
Exception handling and workflow maintenance
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a weekly disruption review that links recurring causes, cost impact and proposed prevention actions, then tracks whether approved changes help.
